newsitem.title: UK: Russian loans continue higher on Paris Club news.
newsitem.headline: Russian loans continue higher on Paris Club news.

text.p: Russian loans were higher on Monday in continued reaction to news on Friday that Russia had been admitted to the Paris Club of creditor nations, emerging market debt experts said.
"Russia is up and that is on a continuation of the developments in Denver," said Richard Gray, emerging market fixed income analyst at Bank of America in London.

Russian loans were also bolstered by comments on Saturday from Russia's first deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais, who said entry into the Paris Club should help Russia get a better credit rating this autumn.
In addition, Chubais said he expected Russia to reach a final agreement with the London Club of commercial bank creditors by the summer.
At 1115 GMT, Russian dollar Vneshekonombank loans were 1/8 higher at 92-5/8 bid, just below record highs of 92-7/8 bid reached earlier today.
Russia is currently rated Ba2 by Moody's Investors Service Inc and BB-minus by Standard and Poor's Corp.
In the broader Eastern European market, traders said Brady bond prices were narrowly mixed in thin trade as many market participants continued to focus on the new issue market.

According to market sources, Poland is expected to issue $300 million of seven-year yankee bonds through lead manager JP Morgan this week, and Croatia is expected to issue 400 million marks via Deutsche Morgan and CS First Boston.
Poland PDI bonds were 1/4 softer at 86-1/2 bid, while Bulgarian IABs were 1/8 firmer at 72-3/8 bid.

In the Latin Brady market, prices were mostly unchanged though Mexican debt could come under pressure heading into the Congressional elections on July 6. Gray, of Bank of America, said he believes Mexico's deteriorating trade accounts coupled with the death of union leader Fidel Velazquez and the upcoming elections, were reasons to lighten up on Mexico.
"There is a combination of deteriorating trade balances and deteriorating politics so...I think there is a case to be light on Mexico," Gray said.
Mexican pars were 1/8 softer at 78-7/8 bid and its discount bonds were unchanged at 93-1/2 bid. Elsewhere, Argentine FRBS were unchanged at 94-1/4 bid and Brazilian IDUs were unchanged at 98-5/8 bid.
